slugline: EXT. CEDAR ROW - LATE AFTERNOON
sound_cue: Distant lawnmower, sparrows, one car approaching and receding, a screen door somewhere
action: The street, flattened by a long lens. Nothing happens for six seconds. A sedan crosses frame left to right and is gone. Hold on the empty street.
qc_note: Hold four seconds past comfort. This is the show's promise: we watch, and we wait.

slugline: EXT. CEDAR ROW - LATE AFTERNOON
sound_cue: Street tone, a dog two gardens away
action: The fourth house. Nothing distinguishes it. A kitchen window on the left side warms as a light is switched on inside.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
sound_cue: Pans, extractor fan off, mail on laminate
action: The kitchen entire. LAUREN at the stove with three pans going, none of them well, entirely happy. MILES leaning against the counter sorting a stack of mail.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
dialogue: MILES: This one's for the Petersens again.
action: MILES, holding up an envelope, not looking up.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
dialogue: LAUREN: Keep it.
action: LAUREN at the stove, over her shoulder.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
dialogue: MILES: It's from a hospital.
action: MILES turns the envelope over.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
dialogue: LAUREN: Then definitely keep it.
action: LAUREN, deadpan, still cooking.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
action: She reaches past him for the salt. Without looking up he shifts his weight out of her way at precisely the right moment. Neither registers it.
qc_note: CONTINUITY-CRITICAL: this is the marriage in one gesture. Do not cut around it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
dialogue: LAUREN: Taste this. | MILES: No. | LAUREN: Taste it.
action: LAUREN turns with a wooden spoon held out.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
dialogue: MILES: I watched you make it.
action: MILES, not moving.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
sound_cue: Room tone, a pan ticking
action: He gives in and tastes it off the spoon. He considers. He considers for noticeably longer than is flattering.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
dialogue: MILES: It's good.
action: MILES, diplomatic.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
dialogue: LAUREN: You hesitated.
action: LAUREN, instantly.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
dialogue: MILES: I was chewing. | LAUREN: It's soup.
action: The two of them.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
action: Beat. Miles laughs - a short exhale through the nose. She goes back to the stove, pleased with herself.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
action: LAUREN crosses to the fridge, takes a pen off a magnet, and adds a line to the notepad stuck there.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
sound_cue: Pen on paper. Nothing else.
action: The notepad. Her handwriting: 'bins - Thurs'. Below it she begins to write a time and forms the numeral 7. The pen lifts, comes back down angled for a cross-stroke through the digit - and stops a quarter-inch short. Hovers. Then lifts away. The seven is left bare.
qc_note: PLANT P3. Pays off on the box label, SC-08. Shoot the abort in one unbroken take.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
action: She caps the pen without ceremony and puts it back on the magnet.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
sound_cue: CHIRP - the episode's signature domestic sound. Establish the exact tone here.
action: The smoke detector on the kitchen ceiling. A single low chirp.
qc_note: PLANT P5. The leaf answers this in SC-17.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - LATE AFTERNOON
dialogue: LAUREN: There it is. | MILES: I'll get a battery. | LAUREN: You've said that. | MILES: And I've meant it every time.
action: Neither of them looks up.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / HALLWAY - CONTINUOUS
action: MILES carries the mail through the narrow hallway, camera following at his shoulder. He passes four bare picture hooks in a row - nails only, and four small pale unfaded rectangles where frames used to hang, or never did.
qc_note: PLANT P1. The hooks must be clearly readable and never remarked on by the camera.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / HALLWAY - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: I'm going to fill those.
action: LAUREN comes out of the kitchen behind him, drying her hands.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / HALLWAY - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: Sure. | LAUREN: I've got the one of the lake. I could get it printed. | MILES: Sure.
action: MILES, walking away, not slowing.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / HALLWAY - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: His footsteps receding. Room tone.
action: LAUREN stops. She looks at the four bare nails for a moment. Then she follows him.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - EVENING
sound_cue: Television dialogue, low and indistinct. Rain has not started yet.
action: The living room. Two lamps and a television playing an old black-and-white film with the sound low. They are folded onto the couch in the way of people who worked out the geometry years ago.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - EVENING
action: On the television: a woman in a coat stands on a railway platform in black and white.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - EVENING
dialogue: MILES: She was never on the train.
action: MILES, quietly, to nobody.
qc_note: PLANT P4. He is three seconds early and does not notice he has done it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - EVENING
action: Three seconds later the detective on screen says something to precisely that effect.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - EVENING
dialogue: LAUREN: How.
action: LAUREN turns her head to look at him.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - EVENING
dialogue: MILES: Lucky guess. | LAUREN: That's four. | MILES: Four what. | LAUREN: You know what. | MILES: I genuinely don't. | LAUREN: Mm.
action: He shrugs it off. She doesn't buy it and doesn't press.
qc_note: Private comedy with no setup. Never explain what the count is.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - EVENING
action: LAUREN reaches for her phone, thumbs the camera open, and lifts it toward him.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - EVENING
dialogue: LAUREN: One picture. | MILES: Absolutely not. | LAUREN: You are a very strange man. | MILES: I photograph poorly.
action: MILES turns his face away - instantly, smoothly, into her shoulder. Played entirely as a joke. It is a reflex wearing a joke's clothes.
qc_note: PLANT P2. Pays off on the camera roll, SC-17.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - EVENING
action: LAUREN lowers the phone, smiling. The smile stays one beat past where it should. Then she puts the phone face-down on the arm of the couch.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - EVENING
sound_cue: Muffled party: bass, laughter, a car door
dialogue: LAUREN: They're doing it again. | MILES: It's Friday.
action: Outside, distantly: music, and people laughing. A party two doors down.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - EVENING
dialogue: LAUREN: We should go over sometime. | MILES: Sure. | LAUREN: That's three sures tonight and you've meant zero of them. | MILES: I mean all of them equally.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - EVENING
dialogue: LAUREN: We're not from around here.
action: LAUREN looks toward the window, and the noise, and the ordinary street.
qc_note: PLANT P9. TITLE DROP, SIDEWAYS. Play it as a bored joke about the neighbours.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - EVENING
sound_cue: The party. Room tone. No score.
action: MILES looks at her. A quarter of a second too long.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - EVENING
dialogue: LAUREN: Them. They're from Ohio. She tells everybody. | MILES: I know what you meant.
action: She indicates the window, meaning the neighbours.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - EVENING
action: MILES holds the look a beat longer than the joke needs. Then he looks away.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / FRONT DOOR - LATER
sound_cue: Deadbolt. Floorboard.
action: MILES at the front door. He turns the deadbolt. Solid. Done. He takes two steps away.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / FRONT DOOR - LATER
sound_cue: Deadbolt, second time. His breath.
action: He comes back and turns it again. Then tests it with the flat of his palm.
qc_note: PLANT P6.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / FRONT DOOR - LATER
action: He leans in to the narrow window beside the door and looks down the street. Left. Then right. Then back to the left, and holds there, longer.
qc_note: PLANT P6. Log this exact sightline; SC-20 uses it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / FRONT DOOR - LATER
action: LAUREN in the hall behind him with a glass of water. She says nothing. She has watched him do this a thousand times.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / FRONT DOOR - LATER
action: She turns back toward the kitchen. As she passes the wall, the camera drifts off her and finds a cheap hardware-store calendar. One date circled in blue ballpoint. Nothing written in the square. She goes past without looking at it - which is its own kind of looking.
qc_note: PLANT P7. The circled date is 14 October. Pays off SC-14.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM & FRONT DOOR - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Television low. Rain begins, very light, on the window.
action: The living room. The film plays. Lauren settles. Miles comes in and sits. For a moment, nothing at all: a warm room and two people in it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM & FRONT DOOR - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: DING-DONG. Loud in the mix. One of only two loud sounds in the episode.
action: THE DOORBELL. Neither of them moves.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM & FRONT DOOR - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Did you order something? | MILES: No. | MILES: Did you? | LAUREN: No.
action: They look at each other. The pause after the second question is far longer than the question deserves.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM & FRONT DOOR - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Chain. Deadbolt. Door seal. Night air and rain.
action: MILES unlocks and opens the door on the chain first. Then all the way.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM & FRONT DOOR - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Rain. The party, two doors down, still going.
action: MILES' POV: the porch is empty. The street is empty. The mat is dark with rain. On the mat, dead centre and squared perfectly to the edge of the step, sits a small brown box.
qc_note: The box's placement is unnaturally precise. Square it to the step with a set square.

slugline: MAIN TITLE
sound_cue: One tone. Then nothing.
action: Black. A single low sustained tone, unresolved, more felt than heard. The main title resolves out of the black letter by letter in thin, wide-tracked type: WE'RE FROM THE FUTURE. The tone stops. The card holds three seconds in total silence. Then it is gone.
qc_note: No stinger. No whoosh. The absence of an impact is the statement.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / ENTRY - NIGHT
sound_cue: Rain outside. The house very quiet.
action: The entry hall. The box sits on the floor where Miles set it down. Neither of them has come closer than four feet. It is small, brown, unbranded, and utterly ordinary, which is the problem.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / ENTRY - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: Don't touch it.
action: MILES.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / ENTRY - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: It's dry.
action: LAUREN is already crouched beside it with her palm flat on the top. She always touches first. It is the whole character.
qc_note: CHARACTER-CRITICAL: she has touched it before he finished the sentence.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / ENTRY - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: What? | LAUREN: It rained. The mat's soaked through. This is dry.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / ENTRY - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: And the corners are perfect. Miles, look at the corners.
action: Her thumb travels along an edge of the box. Every corner is sharp. No crush, no scuff, no thumbprint, no depot smear. It does not look like a thing that has been anywhere.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / ENTRY - NIGHT
sound_cue: Rain. Refrigerator, distantly.
action: He crouches beside her. Looks. Says nothing at all.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
action: The kitchen. They have put the box under the overhead light, on the table, on a folded tea towel - an absurd, careful, entirely domestic instinct.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
action: LAUREN turns the box. On one face: a label.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
action: THE LABEL. White, printed, correct in every visual respect and wrong in every specific one. Their address. No sender. No carrier name, no logo, no service class. There is a barcode - or rather, the SHAPE of a barcode: the bars do not repeat the way bars repeat.
qc_note: Typography must be plausible at a glance and unreadable as a system on inspection.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: There's no company on it. | MILES: There's a barcode. | LAUREN: There's a barcode shape.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
action: Lower on the label, in blue ballpoint, in a small neat hand: '1 of 1', and a six-digit consignment number. The seven in it is crossed.
qc_note: PAYOFF P3. The audience has seen her abort this exact stroke 5 minutes ago. Hold on the crossbar.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
sound_cue: Score out. Refrigerator hum only.
action: LAUREN leans closer. Her eyes travel down to the handwritten line. And she stops. Everything about her stops.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: What? | LAUREN: Nothing. | MILES: Lauren. | LAUREN: It's nothing.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
action: She puts her hand flat over the bottom of the label. Which is not nothing.
qc_note: First lie of the night, and it is HERS. Small, and it matters.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
action: MILES watches her hand. He does not ask again.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: We put it in the car. We drive out to the county road. We leave it.
action: MILES, flat, already planning.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: And then what. | MILES: Then it's somewhere else. | LAUREN: Then it's somewhere else and we come home to this house. Which somebody stood in front of.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
action: He has nothing.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: If someone knows where we live, then the box is the least interesting thing that happened tonight.
action: LAUREN, reasonable, which is worse.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
sound_cue: Compressor kicks in. Rain on glass. Nothing else.
action: A long moment. The refrigerator cycles on. Rain restarts against the window over the sink.
qc_note: Silence #2. Three full seconds with no dialogue and no score.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: Okay. | LAUREN: Okay? | MILES: We open it. And then we talk. Properly. Not the version where you ask and I say it's fine.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: Okay.
action: LAUREN, softer than she was.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
sound_cue: Steel leaving wood.
action: She takes a knife from the block. The good one.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
sound_cue: Tape parting - foregrounded, close-mic'd, almost too loud.
action: The blade goes through the tape. It is a small sound and it is enormous.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
sound_cue: Layered domestic: compressor, rain, distant traffic, tape.
action: She cuts the second seam. The third. Nobody speaks. The refrigerator hums. Rain. A car two streets over.
qc_note: Silence #3. The longest held quiet in Act One.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
sound_cue: CHIRP. Two startled breaths. Two bad laughs.
dialogue: MILES: Battery. | LAUREN: Tomorrow.
action: CHIRP. They both flinch, hard - and then immediately laugh at themselves, badly, with far too much air in it.
qc_note: PAYOFF P5, first stage. The joke version. SC-17 is the other one.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Cardboard.
action: She opens the flaps.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
action: Inside: grey foam, cut to shape. No packing slip, no manual, no plastic, no desiccant. Set into the foam, flat, is the LEAF.
qc_note: HERO REVEAL. It must not read as a tablet. No frame, no bezel, nothing.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Score out. Refrigerator. Rain.
action: Neither of them says anything for a while. It does not look futuristic. It looks finished.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: Don't.
action: MILES, quietly.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: It's heavy. | MILES: It's a screen. | LAUREN: No - Miles, hold it.
action: LAUREN lifts it out of the foam. Two hands.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
action: She holds it out. He takes it two-handed, the way you take something borrowed. It is far heavier than it should be.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: It's moving. | LAUREN: What? | MILES: The weight's moving. Inside it.
action: He adjusts his grip. He tilts the pane slowly. The MASS SHIFTS ACROSS IT - unhurried, a beat behind the motion, like a spirit level, like something settling.
qc_note: DEVICE RULE 3. First impossible physical detail. Achieve in-camera if at all possible.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
action: He sets it down flat on the table. Carefully. He takes his hand off, then puts two fingers back on it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: It's cold. | LAUREN: It's warm.
action: She slides her hand underneath, palm up, against the other face.
qc_note: DEVICE RULE 4: inverted temperature. Cold toward the room, warm away from it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
action: They look at each other.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: It's warm on the bottom. | MILES: It was warm on the bottom before. | LAUREN: Miles. That's a different side.
action: Miles turns the pane over and sets it down again. Lauren touches the top face. Then the underside.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
action: LAUREN sits down. Slowly. Not because she is frightened - because she is thinking, and thinking is what she does with her whole body.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
action: The kitchen is held in the pane. Dimly. The lamp, the cabinets, the shape of her own shoulder.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
action: She raises her hand. The hand in the pane raises - LATE. She lowers it. Raises it again, watching. Down. Up. And the reflection comes with her, a half-beat behind, every time, smooth and unbothered.
qc_note: DEVICE RULE 2 - THE KEY IMAGE OF THE EPISODE. Exactly 0.5s lag. It is not reflecting. It is rendering.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Miles. | MILES: I see it. | LAUREN: Look at my hand. | MILES: I see it, Lauren.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
action: His voice has changed. Flattened. She looks up at him.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Score out entirely.
action: MILES has stopped moving. Completely. Both hands flat on the table. He is not looking at her. He is looking at the pane the way a man looks at a name on a list.
qc_note: CHARACTER-CRITICAL: Miles gets MORE still under fear, never less.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Hey.
action: LAUREN.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Refrigerator. Rain. A held nothing.
action: Nothing. He does not hear her.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: No sound at all. The absence is the effect.
action: THE PANE WAKES. Not an image, not a menu, not a logo. AN EYE - filling the whole surface. Wet. Living. Human. The pupil contracts fractionally in the lamplight. It blinks once. DARK.
qc_note: Under one second on screen. The iris texture must be photographic. Not stylised, not glowing.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
action: The refrigerator hums. Lauren stares at the dead pane. Then, slowly, up at her husband.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
action: MILES has gone white. Absolutely white, from the collar up.
qc_note: The act-out is on his FACE, not on the device. This is a show about people.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Miles? | LAUREN: You know what that is.
action: LAUREN, watching him understand something.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Hard cut to absolute silence.
action: He does not answer. SMASH TO BLACK.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: It's a display unit. It's a demo. Somebody's testing a-
action: MILES moves, fast. He has the box in one hand and is reaching for the pane with the other.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Miles. | MILES: -there's a cell in it, a printed cell, they do that now, it holds a charge for- | LAUREN: Miles.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Score out on the stop.
action: He stops, one hand over the pane.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: You didn't jump.
action: LAUREN.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: What?

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: It turned on. In our kitchen. In the middle of the night. And you didn't jump.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: I jumped. The smoke alarm made me jump. | LAUREN: That thing opened an eye at me and you stood there like you were reading a bill.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: I'm putting it in the car. | LAUREN: No. | MILES: Lauren- | LAUREN: No.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
action: She does not raise her voice. She puts one hand flat on the pane and leaves it there and looks at him. He could move her. They both know he could move her. He does not.
qc_note: BLOCKING-CRITICAL: her hand on the device, his hand withdrawn. The marriage in one frame.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: We agreed. | LAUREN: We didn't agree to this.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: We agreed that if anything ever came near us we don't pick it up, we don't turn it over, we don't keep it in the house-

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: That is not what we agreed. | MILES: It is exactly- | LAUREN: We agreed we wouldn't go looking!
qc_note: First raised voice of the episode. It is hers. It lasts one line.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Refrigerator. Rain. Score out.
dialogue: LAUREN: Nobody ever said what to do when it comes to the door.
action: Back down, immediately.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: Don't be found.
action: MILES, very quiet.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Don't be found. Don't be recorded. Don't go back. Don't answer. Don't send anything forward.
action: LAUREN says it flat and fast, without effort, the way you say a thing you have said ten thousand times.
qc_note: THE TERMS, first full statement. Never explained. Never labelled. Delivered as recitation, not exposition.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: I know them, Miles. I say them at three in the morning. In order. Every night. Have done for six years.
qc_note: PLANT: the double repeats this back to her in SC-11. Place it cleanly.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: Six years.
action: Something crosses him.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Six years and four months, and we have not said one word about any of it out loud in this house, and I have kept that. | LAUREN: I kept it because you asked me to.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: So don't tell me what we agreed.
action: She takes her hand off the pane.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: Where are you going. | LAUREN: I'm putting it on the table where we can see it. | MILES: Don't put it down.
action: She picks the leaf up. Both hands, careful, like a tray.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Pane on wood. Couch. Rain.
action: She puts it down. Flat on the coffee table, dead centre. She sits back on the couch.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: MILES stays standing in the doorway - which is exactly between Lauren and the front hall, and he does not appear to know he has done that. The television is still on, sound low. Nobody is watching it.
qc_note: BLOCKING: ninth instance of Miles interposing himself. Never remarked on.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Television, low and indistinct. Rain. Room tone.
action: Nothing happens. Nothing keeps happening. Lauren pulls a cushion into her lap. Miles shifts his weight.
qc_note: Silence #4. Let it get uncomfortable. The audience must start to relax.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: This is-

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Absolute silence on the wake. Even the television seems to recede.
action: THE LEAF WAKES. No sound, no boot, no logo. The light simply arrives, and it is on their faces. Miles goes silent mid-word.
qc_note: LIGHTING TURN: from here the cold pane is a light source in every living-room shot.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: ON THE PANE: a face in darkness, lit from somewhere low and moving, so that light shifts across it slowly, as if from water. It is LAUREN'S FACE. Same age. Same eyes. Same mouth. Hair down and unstyled. A fine pale scar beneath the left eye, running back along the cheekbone. Old, well healed. She is absolutely still.
qc_note: THE REVEAL. Not monstrous. Not aged. Correct - and too still. That is the entire effect.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Room tone. Rain. No score.
action: LAUREN does not move. Neither does Miles.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: DOUBLE: Lauren.
qc_note: VOICE: Lauren's instrument, flatter, slower, no smile in the timbre. NO BREATH before the line.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: Lauren's hand has gone to her own mouth without her deciding to do it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: DOUBLE: I know. Take a second.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: What is this.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: DOUBLE: You have a burn on the inside of your left wrist. Two inches, curved. | DOUBLE: You got it on a stove that isn't in this house.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: Lauren's other hand closes over her own left wrist.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: DOUBLE: You still say them at three in the morning. | DOUBLE: In order.
qc_note: PAYOFF: she said this two minutes ago in SC-10. Let the audience make the connection unaided.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: One broken intake of breath. Nothing else.
action: LAUREN makes a sound. Not a word.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: Who is this.
action: MILES takes one step into the room.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: The face does not answer him. But she is looking at him. She has been looking at him this entire time.
qc_note: THE DEEPEST REWATCH PAYLOAD. Her eyeline is on MILES in every shot. Never remarked on.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: DOUBLE: You've been here too long.
action: To Lauren.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: What?

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: DOUBLE: It was supposed to be short. Somewhere to be, for a while. | DOUBLE: Six years isn't a while. It's started to hold.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: Hold- | DOUBLE: There's a correction. I don't know how far out it is. I don't think it's far.
action: She talks over him without hurrying.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: A correction of what?

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: DOUBLE: Of the part where you stayed.
qc_note: Hold three seconds of silence after this line. It is the thesis of the season.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: MILES crosses the room fast. He gets one hand flat on the pane - and stops. Because his hand is on it and nothing changes. The face keeps talking. He might as well have put his hand on a wall.
qc_note: DEVICE RULE 5: it does not respond to Miles. Established here, exploited by Lauren in SC-18.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: DOUBLE: Lauren, listen. There's a thing you need to not do, and I need you to hear it from me, because you won't hear it from-

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: How do you have my face?
action: LAUREN, cutting across her.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: DOUBLE: Because I-
action: For the first time, the face hesitates. It is a small thing. Half a second. But it is the first human beat she has had, and it is horrible, because it means she is deciding what to say.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Rain, distorted. Somebody off-frame shouting a name that is not Miles and is not Lauren.
action: THE FOOTAGE. Degraded, narrow, recovered-looking. Night, outdoors, hard rain in a hard light. MILES and LAUREN, older - not much, enough. Moving fast, not running: escorting, one holding the other up. Miles has blood in his hairline and down the side of his face. Behind them, badly out of focus and high up, a sodium-yellow SIGN with half a word legible.
qc_note: UNDER FOUR SECONDS. Cut on movement. Never let a face resolve fully. The SIGN pays off in SC-18.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Television. Rain. Nothing else.
action: BLACK. The pane is dead. The room is dark except for the television, still playing its old film to nobody. Neither of them moves.
qc_note: Silence #5.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: There was a sign.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: There wasn't.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Behind us. Yellow. Up high. | MILES: Lauren, it was three seconds of- | LAUREN: There was a sign, Miles.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: And you saw it. Because you stopped breathing.
action: She turns and looks at him properly for the first time since it started.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Rain. Television credits music, thin and far away.
action: He does not answer. He does not answer for a long time. Rain on the window. The film ends and the credits roll, silently, on a television nobody is watching.
qc_note: Silence #6, and the longest in the act. Hold on his face until it is unbearable.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: CHIRP. Then a hard cut to absolute silence.
action: CHIRP. Cut to black and total silence.
qc_note: ACT OUT. The chirp is the last sound. No stinger.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / VARIOUS - NIGHT
sound_cue: Drawer runners. His breathing. Nothing else.
action: No music. Almost no sound. Just a man working. MILES slides the pane face-down into the bottom drawer of the sideboard and shuts it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / VARIOUS - NIGHT
action: He stands there. Then he reaches out and touches the brass drawer pull. It is cold. He takes his hand back.
qc_note: Containment failure #1. No effect, no sound. A cold handle. That is all.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / VARIOUS - NIGHT
action: He puts it in a camping cooler. Clips the lid. Stands back. Then, slowly, he puts his palm flat on the lid. It is warm.
qc_note: Containment failure #2.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / VARIOUS - NIGHT
sound_cue: Breaker. Then the entire sound bed of the house stops. This is the quietest moment in the episode.
action: He goes to the breaker panel in the hall closet and throws the main. The house dies - refrigerator, television, the lamp in the hall, all of it, gone at once.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / VARIOUS - NIGHT
action: He comes back to the living room in the dark. The pane is lying on the coffee table where Lauren has put it back. It is glowing.
qc_note: Containment failure #3, and the reason the audience now believes the rules.

slugline: EXT. CEDAR ROW - NIGHT
sound_cue: Rain. Party. A dog. Traffic on a main road four streets away.
action: The street. Every house has its lights on except one. A dog barks twice somewhere. A television flickers blue through a window. Two doors down the party is still going: laughter, a car door, somebody calling somebody else an idiot with enormous affection. The world is completely, insultingly fine.
qc_note: The only exterior in Act Three. It exists to make the house smaller.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
action: Power back on, one lamp. LAUREN sits in the armchair facing the coffee table. She has put Miles's canvas jacket over the pane. She has not moved in a while. Miles comes in and stands.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: I know what it is. | MILES: Not who sent it. I don't know that. But I know what it is.
action: She does not look up.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: You've seen one. | MILES: I've held one. | LAUREN: When?

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
sound_cue: Lamp hum. Rain. Score out.
action: He does not answer.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: Okay. | LAUREN: Then here's the one I actually want.
action: LAUREN, not being generous. Filing it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: Why me? It knows my wrist. It knows what I do at three in the morning. | LAUREN: It's got my face, Miles. Why does it want me and not you?
action: She looks up.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
action: Miles opens his mouth. Nothing comes out.
qc_note: Silence #7.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
action: Lauren watches his hands go flat on the back of the couch. She has seen that before too.
qc_note: MILES'S TELL, established in the character bible. This is its first on-screen naming.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: Where are you-
action: She gets up, crosses to the table, lifts the jacket and takes the label out from under the pane where she left it. She reads it. Then she walks out of the room.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
sound_cue: Refrigerator. Rain. Absolutely no dialogue.
action: LAUREN stops in front of the wall calendar. The circled date. Blue pen. Nothing written in it. She looks down at the label in her hand. She looks up at the calendar. She stands there a long time.
qc_note: THE BEST PASSAGE IN THE ACT. Fourteen seconds of a woman doing arithmetic. Do not cover it in dialogue. Do not cut away.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: What happens on the fourteenth.
action: She comes back in with the label held up between two fingers.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: Nothing.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: It's on the box, Miles. It's the consignment date. | LAUREN: And it's the one day of the year you circle on a calendar and don't write anything in.
qc_note: PAYOFF P7.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: Six years I've watched you circle that. I never asked. | LAUREN: I decided it was somebody's birthday, and that you'd tell me when you could.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: So tell me when you can.
action: She lowers the label.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
sound_cue: Score out.
action: MILES sits down on the arm of the couch. It takes him a moment to do it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: Once a year. | LAUREN: Once a year what. | MILES: I send nine words.
qc_note: THE CONFESSION. Play it as small as possible. He is not confessing; he is being drained.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
sound_cue: Rain. Nothing else.
action: The room is very quiet.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: You send. | MILES: Yes. | LAUREN: Forward. | MILES: Yes. | LAUREN: That's five. | MILES: I know what it is. | LAUREN: Say it. | MILES: That's clause five.
action: One syllable at a time.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: How many times. | MILES: Six.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
action: LAUREN turns away from him. All the way around, hands on top of her head, looking at nothing.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: What are the nine words. | MILES: Lauren- | LAUREN: What are the nine words, Miles.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: We're still here. We're okay. Don't come. I'm sorry.
action: MILES.
qc_note: THE NINE WORDS. Absolutely flat. He has said them six times into a void and they have worn smooth.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: Who's I'm sorry for? | LAUREN: Who is it for?
action: She turns back.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: There's somebody who thinks we didn't make it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: Who. | MILES: Lauren. | LAUREN: Who?

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
sound_cue: Score out. Rain.
action: He cannot. He physically cannot get it out. His mouth works and nothing comes.
qc_note: The name is never spoken in this episode. It arrives as a voice in SC-22 instead.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: Oh.
action: And Lauren - watching him fail - understands something, and goes absolutely still.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
action: She looks down at the label in her hand. At the crossed seven. At the date.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: Miles. | LAUREN: You didn't get a package. | MILES: Don't. | LAUREN: You got an answer.
action: THE TURN.
qc_note: THE PIVOT OF THE EPISODE. Quiet. No music. She is not accusing him; she is solving it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: Lauren- | LAUREN: YOU PUT OUR ADDRESS IN THE AIR ONCE A YEAR FOR SIX YEARS AND LET ME THINK I WAS SAFE!
action: It rips out of her. It is the loudest thing in this house in six years and it is over in two seconds.
qc_note: THE LOUDEST HUMAN SOUND IN THE EPISODE. One line. Then the silence afterward is enormous.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
sound_cue: Total silence for two seconds after her line.
action: Miles has not moved.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: It's nine words. There's no address in it. There's no- | LAUREN: There's a when.
action: Low.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: Every year. Same day. Same time, I'd bet. | LAUREN: You didn't tell them where we are. You told them we're regular.
action: That stops him.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
action: Miles puts his hand over his mouth and holds it there.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: They didn't find us. You waved.
qc_note: The cruellest line in the episode and she does not raise her voice for it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
sound_cue: Rain. Refrigerator. Score out.
action: Long silence.
qc_note: Silence #8. Separated framing: they are at opposite ends of the widest lens in the room.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: They told us nobody would come looking. | LAUREN: They told us a lot of things.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: They said the whole point - the entire point, Lauren, the reason for all of it, | MILES: the reason we don't have photographs and I check a street I have checked eleven thousand times - | MILES: was that if we did it properly, nobody would ever have to come.
qc_note: PAYOFF P1. The picture hooks are explained here, in an argument, at speed, and never returned to.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: And you did it properly. | MILES: I did it properly for three hundred and sixty-four days a year.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: Yeah.
action: She sits down on the coffee table, right beside the covered pane, because her legs have stopped being interested.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: I'm not angry that you lied. | MILES: You are. | LAUREN: I'm a little angry that you lied.
action: Almost - almost - the ghost of the two people from the beginning of the evening. Then it is gone.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: You didn't protect me, Miles. | LAUREN: You just made sure that when it came, I'd be the one who was surprised.
action: The thesis of the marriage.
qc_note: THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THE EPISODE. It must be the QUIETEST. No music under it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
sound_cue: Rain. Nothing else.
action: He has no answer to that. There isn't one.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: The room has just got colder. You can see it: her arms come in. She gets up, takes a grey cardigan off the back of the chair, and pulls it on.
qc_note: WARDROBE CHANGE WRD-L-A -> WRD-L-B. Cold is a device rule, not a mood. Log to continuity.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: It does that. | LAUREN: Does what. | MILES: When it's about to.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: Lauren. | LAUREN: Don't. | MILES: Lauren.
action: She looks at him. Six years of not asking, and now every single answer is a new injury.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: She stops. He comes over. He does not touch her. He gets close enough to.
qc_note: FIRST SHARED FRAME SINCE 20:15. The reunion is aborted, but the framing is the promise.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: I have been so scared for so long that I forgot it was a thing that could end. | MILES: I thought if I could just hold it - for long enough-
action: The only articulate thing Miles says all night.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Rain. Two people breathing. Nothing else.
action: He raises his hand and puts it on her arm, just above the elbow. She lets him. Ten seconds of two people almost, almost getting back.
qc_note: Silence #9. The near-repair. It must be genuinely tender or the interruption is worthless.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: No sound. Light only.
action: LIGHT. The pane, under the jacket, comes on so brightly that the canvas glows from underneath.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: Miles pulls the jacket off.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: ON THE PANE: no face. A black field. Four words in thin white wide-tracked type. DO NOT GO BACK.
qc_note: Typography must match the main title card exactly. That is the point: it is the same house style.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Okay. That's what you've been saying. That's what you've been saying all night. | LAUREN: Stay put. Do nothing. That's good, isn't it-
action: Lauren stares at it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: She turns to him. MILES has taken a step BACK from the table. Not a flinch - a retreat. He has put distance between himself and four words on a screen and he is looking at them like they are a person in the room.
qc_note: THE ACT'S REAL TURN. He is not reacting to the content. He is reacting to the grammar.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Miles? | MILES: That's not advice. | LAUREN: What? | MILES: That's not somebody warning us. That's - Lauren, that's word for word.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: That's clause three.
action: She looks at the screen. Then at him. And then she gets it, and it takes all the blood out of her too.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Somebody over there is reading us our own Terms. | MILES: Somebody over there has them.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: A filtered noise pulse arrives on each second. Felt more than heard.
action: Beneath the four words, small, precise, unhurried, a number appears. 11:00. It becomes 10:59. Then 10:58.
qc_note: THE COUNTDOWN BEGINS. From here it runs in real time and reaches 00:00 at the knock in SC-22.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Down to what.
action: Very quietly.
qc_note: ACT OUT. Cut to black on her face, not on the number.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
action: Overhead light on. Everything visible. Two people working. There is no panic in this room, and that is the frightening part.
qc_note: Their competence IS the horror. Nobody hurries. Nobody drops anything.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: Back door, alley, left, and you're on Weir in ninety seconds. | MILES: Front door, you're on Cedar, and Cedar only goes two ways.
action: Lauren has a pad and is writing a list in fast legible capitals. Miles is at the back door.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: Car? | MILES: Car's on Cedar. | LAUREN: So the car's decorative. | MILES: The car's a place somebody would wait.
action: He says it the way you'd say the milk's off.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
action: He goes to the hall closet, reaches up past the coats, and takes down two canvas duffels. They are grey with dust across the top.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: How long have those been up there? | MILES: Since we moved in. | LAUREN: Six years. | MILES: Yes. | LAUREN: You packed one for me. | MILES: I packed two.
action: Lauren stares at them.
qc_note: Complicating grace note: he DID prepare for her. He just never told her.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
action: She unzips hers. Cash in a band. A phone still in its box. Socks. A folding knife. A coat she does not remember owning. And at the bottom, face-down, a small photograph.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: We're not allowed to have this. | MILES: I know.
action: She turns it over. We do not see it. She looks at it for a long moment.
qc_note: PAYOFF P1 / clause two. NEVER show the photograph. Not this season.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
action: She puts it in her back pocket.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
sound_cue: Phone buzz on laminate.
action: Her phone buzzes on the counter. She picks it up. Reads it. Then stops.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
action: THE PHONE. A message from no one. Blank body. Received: 3:14 AM. The clock at the top of the screen reads 11:26 PM.
qc_note: Impossibility #1. Give the audience three full seconds to do the subtraction themselves.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
dialogue: MILES: Okay. | LAUREN: Okay? | MILES: I'm putting it in the drawer.
action: She turns the phone around and shows him. He looks at it for two full seconds.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
action: He takes the phone, opens a drawer, puts it in, and closes it. It is such a calm, useless, human thing to do that Lauren almost laughs.
qc_note: The episode's only laugh in the back half. It must be almost, and it must be sad.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
sound_cue: The refrigerator compressor stutters once, on the repeat.
action: The microwave clock. 11:26. It becomes 11:25. Then it sits there. And then, without hurrying, it goes back to 11:25 again - the same minute twice, four seconds of a night happening a second time.
qc_note: Impossibility #2. Neither of them says one word about it. That restraint is the scene.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - NIGHT
dialogue: LAUREN: Money, coats, the label. What else. | MILES: Nothing else. That's the whole point of the bags.
action: They both see it. Neither says anything. Lauren picks up her list. Her hand is not entirely steady. She keeps writing.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
action: She goes to reach for her phone in the drawer - stops herself - takes it out anyway. She opens the camera roll to check something. And her thumb stops moving.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
action: THE PHONE. The most recent photograph: the living room of this house, tonight - the lamp in tonight's position, the jacket on the arm of the couch. MILES and LAUREN, asleep, folded together on the couch. Taken from across the room. From the doorway.
qc_note: Impossibility #3, and PAYOFF P2. The most frightening image in the episode is a photograph of them sleeping.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: When. | LAUREN: Tonight. That's the lamp. That's your jacket. | MILES: We didn't sleep tonight. | LAUREN: No.
action: Lauren holds the phone out to him without a word. Miles looks.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Score out.
action: They look at each other.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: CHIRP - identical to SC-02.
action: CHIRP. The smoke detector above them. Same as it has been all week.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: CHIRP from off-screen right, spatially placed in the living room. Half a beat late.
action: And then, from the living room: CHIRP. The same tone. The same length. A half-beat late.
qc_note: PAYOFF P5. This is the moment the house stops being a house.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
action: Miles goes to the doorway and looks through into the dark living room. The pane is lying face-up on the coffee table. It is black. The countdown is not showing. It is doing nothing at all.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: CHIRP, sourced precisely at the coffee table. Then absolute silence.
action: CHIRP. It comes from the pane, while he is standing there looking at it, and there is nothing on it to make a sound.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: It won't do anything for you. | MILES: What? | LAUREN: You put your whole hand on it and it kept talking. I walk past it, it wakes up.
action: Lauren comes in behind him.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: Lauren. | LAUREN: I know.
action: She crouches down in front of the coffee table. Level with the pane.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: That's four. Don't answer it. That's four, Lauren, that's the one you've never- | LAUREN: And five's yours. So we're even.
qc_note: LAUREN BREAKS A CLAUSE TOO. The marriage is now symmetrical. This is deliberate.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: That lands. He stops.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Rain. Nothing. Nothing.
dialogue: LAUREN: If you want us to do something, show me where.
action: She looks at the black pane.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Held silence, five seconds.
action: Nothing. Nothing.
qc_note: Make the audience believe it isn't going to answer.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: THE STILL. Night, rain. A low, long two-storey motel beside a state highway. External walkway, twelve doors, sodium light. A tall yellow pole sign with one dead letter: BLU RIDG MOT L. Held. Four seconds. Gone. Black.
qc_note: PAYOFF: this is the sign from the SC-11 footage. Same sign, same dead letter.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: That's the sign. Miles, that's the sign from the - that's the sign.
action: Lauren is on her feet.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Miles. What is it?
action: He is not looking at the pane. He is looking at the middle distance, and he has gone somewhere else entirely.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: That's where we came in.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: What? | MILES: Room eleven. Second floor, end of the walkway. That's the crossing.
action: He says the largest thing he has said all night the way you'd say a street name.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: I don't remember that. | MILES: No. | LAUREN: Miles, I don't remember any of that. | MILES: I know.
qc_note: A SPENT MYSTERY REPLACED BY A BETTER ONE. This is the episode's most important structural move.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: And I have never once known what to do with that.
action: He finally looks at her.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Score thins to one piano note.
action: Lauren stands in the middle of her own living room and feels the floor go.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: It told us not to go back. | MILES: Yes. | LAUREN: And then it showed us where to go. | MILES: Yes. | LAUREN: So one of those is a lie. | MILES: Yes. | LAUREN: Which one? | MILES: I don't know.
action: The contradiction lands.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: DOUBLE: Lauren.
action: THE PANE COMES ON. The face again, closer than before, filling more of the frame. Steady. Tired. Kind.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: Lauren does not answer her.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: DOUBLE: I'm going to say something, and it's going to be unkind, and I'm sorry, and I'd do it again.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: DOUBLE: Count backwards for me. I'll be here at one.
qc_note: THE BREAK. Deliver it warmly. It is a mother's line and she means it kindly.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Score out entirely. Rain. Her breathing.
action: Lauren's face comes apart. It is not a scream and it is not tears. It is the specific and terrible expression of a person hearing, in their own voice, out of a machine, a sentence that has only ever existed in one room in the world - and that room does not exist yet.
qc_note: THE PERFORMANCE HIGH POINT OF THE EPISODE. Hold. Do not cut away for comfort.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: She sits down on the floor. Her hand goes to the pendant at her throat and closes around it. A reflex much older than her marriage.
qc_note: CONTINUITY: first appearance of the pendant reflex. Logged in the character bible.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: My mother said that. | MILES: Lauren- | LAUREN: My mother said that to me. Every night. Nobody knows that.
action: Barely audible.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: I have never said that out loud. Not once. Not here. Not to him.
action: She looks up at the screen.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: DOUBLE: I know. | DOUBLE: She said it to me too.
action: The double's face does something small and very sad.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: CRITICAL: the audio bed itself stops for 0.5s. Room tone, rain, everything. Then resumes.
dialogue: DOUBLE: Didn't she, [ - - - ]
action: Her mouth makes a name. Two syllables. It is not Lauren. And where the sound should be there is a clean, absolute, half-second ABSENCE. Not a bleep. Not static. A hole.
qc_note: Do NOT bleep, mute, distort or cover with a sound. REMOVE the audio. The absence must be authored.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: What did you just call her.
action: Miles's head snaps around. He heard it. Or heard the shape of it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: The double does not answer him. She never has. But she is looking at him.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: What am I? | DOUBLE: You're the one who-
action: Lauren gets up, unsteady.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM & WINDOW - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: The entire sound bed cuts. This is the second and last loud moment: the SILENCE is the impact.
action: BLACK. Every light in the house goes out at once. The refrigerator stops. The microwave clock dies. The whole building drops into darkness in a single beat.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM & WINDOW - CONTINUOUS
action: Lauren freezes. Miles goes straight to the window and pulls the curtain aside two inches.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM & WINDOW - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Muffled through glass: the party, warm and completely indifferent.
action: MILES' POV: the street. Every porch light on. Every window lit. The party two doors down still going, warm and yellow and loud. Every house on the street has power.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM & WINDOW - CONTINUOUS
action: Behind Miles, on the coffee table, the pane is glowing steadily. It is the only light in the house.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM & WINDOW - CONTINUOUS
action: Miles looks out along the street - left, right, and then back to the left. To the same spot he checks every night of his life.
qc_note: PAYOFF P6. Same sightline as SC-05.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM & WINDOW - CONTINUOUS
action: There is a FIGURE standing at the edge of the streetlight's throw. Not close. Not moving.
qc_note: Soft, small in frame, absolutely still. No detail. Do not silhouette dramatically.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM & WINDOW - CONTINUOUS
action: Miles turns his head fully to look at it directly.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM & WINDOW - CONTINUOUS
action: There is nobody there.
qc_note: No whip-pan. No sting. Just an empty pavement, held one beat too long.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM & WINDOW - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Rain. The party. His breathing.
action: He does not move for a long moment.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM & WINDOW - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: The brass mechanism, close-mic'd, unhurried. The single most important sound effect in the episode.
action: From the front hall, very clearly, in a completely silent house: THE DEADBOLT TURNS. One full revolution.
qc_note: ACT OUT. Nobody touches it. Cut to black on the sound, not after it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: Dark. The pane is the only light in the world and it is the wrong colour for a home. Neither of them screams. Neither of them runs.
qc_note: THE THESIS OF ACT FIVE: they are competent, and it is worse.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Chair legs on carpet, then on board.
action: Miles crosses the room, takes the armchair by the back, and drags it - quietly, without hurry - into the mouth of the hallway. Not a barricade. An obstacle. A thing to trip on in the dark.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: Lauren shoulders her bag, picks up the pane, wraps it in the cardigan and puts it in the bag. Then she takes the fire iron from the hearth and puts it on the coffee table where either of them can reach it.
qc_note: She arms them both. She does not hand him the iron; she puts it where either can take it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: They move around each other in the dark like people who have done a drill. Because they have.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: Back door. | LAUREN: No. | MILES: Lauren, the alley's clear, you go left and you're- | LAUREN: No. | MILES: Please.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: I'm not doing the part where you decide for me twice in one night.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: That's not what this is. | LAUREN: That's exactly what this is. | LAUREN: You've done it for six years. It's the only thing you're actually good at.
action: That stops him dead.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Miles. We're doing this one together or we're not doing it.
action: Gentler, and worse.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: Okay. | LAUREN: Okay.
action: He looks at her in the light off the bag.
qc_note: WARDROBE: jacket is now on. WRD-M-B from here to end.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: She checks the pane through the fabric. The number is showing through the weave. 01:20. 01:19.
qc_note: COUNTDOWN CHECK: this must read 01:20 at exactly 1:20 before the knock. Bound in the EDL.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: There's something you need to know before that gets to zero. | LAUREN: Then say it fast.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: Nobody comes over. | LAUREN: What? | MILES: It's not against the rules. It's - Lauren, it isn't a rule, it's a fact.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: People don't cross. Things don't cross. | LAUREN: We crossed. | MILES: We came out. That's different. That's falling. Anyone can fall.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: Coming the other way costs something. It costs more than a person has. | LAUREN: Meaning what. | MILES: Meaning nothing comes through whole.
action: He is not trying to frighten her. He is telling her a load-bearing fact about the world, and he is terrified.
qc_note: THE SERIES' DARKEST RULE. Six words. Never elaborated this season.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: MILES: So whatever is out there - whatever it used to be - it paid everything it had to stand on our step. | MILES: And it did that on purpose. And it did it tonight.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: The number in the bag: 00:41.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Miles, I have to ask you something and I need you to not manage me. | MILES: Okay.
action: Lauren stares at him in the dark.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Score out. Absolute silence under the question.
dialogue: LAUREN: That message. | LAUREN: Did it come from me?

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: Miles opens his mouth. He does not lie to her. He genuinely, visibly, does not lie to her. He also does not say anything. Three seconds.
qc_note: THE MOST IMPORTANT PAUSE IN THE EPISODE. Three full seconds. Hold it.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Okay.
action: That is the answer, and she takes it standing up.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: LIGHT. Inside the bag, through the cardigan, the pane brightens. Lauren pulls it out.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: THE DOUBLE. Closer than she has ever been. Her face nearly fills the pane. She is looking straight out - and her eyes are not on Lauren. They are on Miles. Where they have been all night.
qc_note: THE PAYLOAD. Do not underline it. Do not rack focus to Miles. Just let her eyeline be wrong.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Who are you?

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Score out on 'Don't'. Nothing under it.
dialogue: DOUBLE: I'm the one who left when they told me to. | DOUBLE: Don't.
action: And for the first time in the entire episode, the double looks away from Miles. She looks at Lauren.
qc_note: She is not a threat. She is evidence of what obedience cost. Play it as grief.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: The number, small, beneath her face. 00:04. 00:03. 00:02. 00:01. 00:00.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: TOTAL SILENCE. No rain, no room tone, nothing. The mix floor drops to zero.
action: Nothing happens. The house is silent. The pane holds her face, perfectly still, waiting with them.
qc_note: Eight seconds of nothing after zero. The audience must conclude it is over.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Five knuckle knocks on a wooden door, unhurried, patterned. Dry. No reverb tail.
action: KNOCK. KNOCK. KNOCK. A pause. KNOCK. KNOCK. Three, then two.
qc_note: It is not a stranger's knock. It has a shape. A private meaning between two people.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
action: Miles's head comes up. And everything in his face falls apart at once - not fear. Not fear at all. RECOGNITION.
qc_note: THE EPISODE LIVES OR DIES HERE. Hold on him. It is the answer to who he has been writing to.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
dialogue: LAUREN: Miles. | LAUREN: Miles, what.
action: Watching him.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Through a wooden door and a wall. Warm. Kind. Utterly unhurried. Gender deliberately unclear.
dialogue: VOICE (O.S.): It's me.
action: And from outside - through the door, muffled, unhurried, and warm.
qc_note: Two syllables. They must sound like an embrace. That is why it is frightening.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: Nothing at all.
action: Miles closes his eyes.

slugline: INT. WARD HOUSE / LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
sound_cue: One tone, low, and then nothing. Rain returns very faintly at the last second.
action: FINAL SHOT. The dark house. The two of them side by side at last, shoulder against shoulder, lit from below by a pane of glass that should not exist. Behind them, deep in frame, the front door - its frosted panel a soft rectangle of streetlight. Something on the other side moves: a shift of weight, a change in the light, a shape that is a person and is not quite the right size for a person. It does not resolve. The deadbolt is already open.
qc_note: THE ONLY SHARED FRAME SINCE 20:15. It cost them the entire episode to stand next to each other. CUT TO BLACK BEFORE THE DOOR OPENS.

slugline: END CARD
sound_cue: The main-title tone returns, resolved a semitone lower. Then out.
action: Black. Silence. Then, thin and wide-tracked: WE'RE FROM THE FUTURE. Below it, smaller: END OF EPISODE ONE.

slugline: INT. A PALE ROOM - NO TIME GIVEN
sound_cue: Room tone with no reflections in it - an acoustically dead space. Deeply wrong.
action: A room lit uniformly from everywhere, so that nothing casts a shadow and no corner can be located. A FIGURE stands at a waist-height surface, seen from behind and below the shoulders. We will not see their face.

slugline: INT. A PALE ROOM - NO TIME GIVEN
action: They hold a flat unlit sheet, roughly the size and thickness of the pane. On it: two records side by side. No photographs. Designations that do not resolve as language. The first record's status field reads LOST.
qc_note: The sheet is a leaf. Same object, institutional context. Never say so.

slugline: INT. A PALE ROOM - NO TIME GIVEN
sound_cue: No confirmation sound. Nothing acknowledges it.
action: The figure touches it, once. LOST becomes LOCATED.

slugline: INT. A PALE ROOM - NO TIME GIVEN
action: They move to the second record. Its status field ALREADY reads LOCATED. Beside it, a date. It is nineteen years old.
qc_note: THE TAG'S ENTIRE PURPOSE. Nineteen years. Hold long enough to read it and no longer.

slugline: INT. A PALE ROOM - NO TIME GIVEN
action: The figure stops. Just stops. The only human thing that happens in this room.

slugline: INT. A PALE ROOM - NO TIME GIVEN
sound_cue: Flat, female, pleasant, unhurried. No processing. It sounds like a lift announcement.
dialogue: SYSTEM VOICE: Retrieval is already in progress.
qc_note: BLACK on the last syllable. No music. No sting.
